newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression heads towards Texas.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression heads towards Texas.

text.p: The 10th tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season headed slowly northeast through the Gulf of Mexico on Saturday, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT) the center of the depression was estimated near latitude 23.9 north and longitude 95.5 west or about 185 miles (296 km) southeast of Brownsville, Texas.

It was moving northeastwards near seven mph (11 kph), with maximum sustained winds of 35 mph (55 kph). It was expected to keep going in the same direction and possibly strengthen into a tropical storm, the center said.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph) and gain hurricane status when winds hit 74 mph (119 kph).
The depression would be named Josephine if it strengthened into a tropical storm.
